BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on nearly every material point. Several positions sit at or beyond our conditional fallbacks, and the Seller's "FINAL / not to be re-opened" framing is not a basis for accepting them. Our playbook controls. We have no record of Amelia Frost's written authority for any of these positions, so none should be treated as agreed.

**Caveats:**
- We have the Seller's *summary* of the SPA and a disclosure letter. We do not have the full SPA text. The clause cross-references (e.g., 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) need checking against the actual draft.
- The disclosure letter is dated to the data room as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026, so the record is about six weeks stale. Bluefen, Riverlark and the DD-006 investigation may have moved. We need a current data room index and bring-down.

---

## 1. Liability and Limits

**General cap (cl 12.1).** Seller: 20% / AUD 4.8m. Playbook: start at 25% / AUD 6m. The 20% / AUD 4.8m figure is a conditional fallback that requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None has been given.
- *Push back:* Open at AUD 6m and do not offer 20% without written authority.
- The Seller's "10–20% is market" argument does not change our position.

**De minimis and basket (cl 12.2).** Seller: AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket with excess-only recovery. Playbook: AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 aggregate basket with first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
- The Seller's basket is five times ours and works as a deductible, not a tipping basket. Combined with the de minimis, it would bar most realistic small claims.
- *Push back:* AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 tipping basket from the first dollar.

**Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13).** Seller: 18 months for general claims, plus a global clause that any limitation applies to *all* claims unless expressly excluded. Playbook: 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost's written approval (none given).
- The global "applies to all claims" language is the more serious problem. It would sweep Title, Fundamental, Tax, IP and fraud into the general regime by default, which is a hidden override.
- *Push back:* Reject the global override. Keep 24 months for general claims. Specify separate periods for each category.

**Fundamental / Title (cl "Fundamental / Title").** Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the general caps and time limits "for simplicity." Playbook: separate regime; 100% cap; at least six years; outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- This is a clear departure. Title and capacity are the core of what we are buying.
- *Push back:* Reject. Title and capacity sit in a separate regime as set out in the playbook.

**Exclusive remedy, non-reliance and limitations (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).** Seller: these apply to all claims of any nature. The fraud carve-out is absent.
- *Push back:* Carve out fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one on either side may waive this. This is a non-negotiable.

---

## 2. Disclosure and Buyer Knowledge

**General disclosure (Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2; Schedule 7).** The Seller discloses everything in the data room (including DD-002 to DD-012), the accounts, statutory registers and public records. Playbook: reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure; require specific fair disclosure.
- This makes the specific disclosures in sections 2–10 of the letter largely meaningless, because it would deem disclosed anything in the data room.
- *Push back:* Delete 1.1 and 1.2 and the reliance on the data room in Schedule 7. Accept only specific, fairly disclosed items. Note that the specific disclosures in the letter are the right form; the general language is what needs removing.
- Also note 1.4 (no admissions) should not be allowed to affect specific indemnities or warranty breach determinations.

**Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** Seller: no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. Playbook: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must use named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- The "discoverable" wording is a constructive-knowledge bar in disguise.
- *Push back:* Delete cl 8.3. If the Seller insists on a knowledge qualifier, limit it to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, with the carve-outs above.

---

## 3. Conditions and Completion Mechanics

**Bluefen (cl 3 / 6.3; Disclosure §2).** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or about 30% of FY26 revenue. Consent is not yet obtained, and the Seller has not evidenced that the conditions in clause 11.3 are satisfied. The Seller proposes reasonable endeavours and treating consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- This departs from the playbook on two counts: consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours. The playbook says reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- *Push back:* Make effective Bluefen consent a condition precedent, and require evidence that its clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion. If the Seller cannot deliver that, we need a walk right, price protection or a specific indemnity. Those alternatives are my suggestions, not playbook positions, so they need principal sign-off.

**Riverlark (cl 2 / 7; Disclosure §3).** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. The facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included. The Seller proposes a release "following Completion."
- This is the reverse of the playbook. Direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases are required.
- *Push back:* Require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective releases at Completion. A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- Note: under the debt-free/cash-free mechanics, this is a Debt item. Leaving it unpaid at Completion shifts the cost to us.

---

## 4. Funds Flow and Specific Items

**Employee bonuses (DD-005; Disclosure §5; funds flow).** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses are not in the funds flow. Payroll tax and super on-costs are unquantified. The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller" but does not itemise or fund them.
- *Push back:* Add the bonuses to the funds flow as a specific line item, or have the Seller fund them. Require the Seller to quantify the on-costs and make them part of that line item or seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.

**Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DD-004, DD-010; Disclosure §4).** The Seller says the indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000) and is "adequate." The DD-004 clause 7.3 condition on transfer of Project Materials means the risk is broader than the fee. There is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified.
- *Push back:* Broaden the indemnity beyond the fee to cover defects in the IP transfer. Preserve the SOW3 cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment before Completion). Verify the AUD 180,000 independently, in both directions: the Seller may have paid, or the amount may be wrong.

**Export/privacy incident (DD-006; cl 4.6 / Schedule 6; Disclosure §6).** The Seller calls it a "preliminary operational matter" and says it is not expected to be material. The material does not establish unauthorised access, scope or notification duty. About 1,240 records are involved.
- The playbook says to assume neither a confirmed breach nor harm, and not to assume a numeric demand either way. The Seller's "not material" characterisation should not be accepted as a basis for ignoring the matter.
- *Push back:* Require preservation of logs, a completed investigation, defined scope and regular written updates. Keep the matter outside the general regime, consistent with the no-override rule.
- My suggestion, beyond the playbook: consider a specific indemnity for incident-related costs, since the investigation is still open. This needs principal sign-off.

**Sandbar renewals (DD-008, DD-011; Disclosure §8; AUD 330,000).** The Seller calls them ordinary-course operating costs. The playbook says to assess them and not automatically treat them as Debt or deduct from price.
- *Push back:* Do not accept the ordinary-course label without evidence. Assess whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or related to the others. Do not make an automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

---

## 5. Open Categories

**Tax and IP (Seller update).** The Seller considers these "settled under the general regime." The playbook says Tax and IP terms remain **open**, and we should assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- *Push back:* Reject the folding of Tax and IP into the general regime. Keep them as separate categories and state that they remain open. Do not concede unlimited liability.

**Title (DD-012; Disclosure §10).** The Seller relies on the company share register as evidence of title. The playbook says DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof.
- *Push back:* Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. Suggested sources: ASIC company extract, PPSR search, and verified transfer and authority documents. These are my suggestions for meeting the playbook requirement.

**Mossvale and office lease (DD-009, DD-007; Disclosure §7, §9).** The Seller states that neither the Mossvale assignment restriction nor the lease notification obligation requires consent merely because the shares are sold. This is not a playbook item, but we should verify it against the underlying contracts.

---

## 6. Summary of Recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our position | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | 25% / 6m; 20% only with written Frost authority | High |
| 2 | De minimis / basket | 25k / 250k excess-only | 5k / 50k tipping | High |
| 3 | Time limits | 18m; global override | 24m; reject global override | High |
| 4 | Title / Fundamental | General caps and limits | 100%; 6+ years; separate regime | Critical |
| 5 | Fraud carve-out | Absent | Full carve-out; non-waivable | Critical |
| 6 | Data-room disclosure | Whole data room deemed disclosed | Delete; specific disclosure only | Critical |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket bar incl. discoverable | Delete | High |
| 8 | Bluefen | Endeavours; consent on delivery | CP with evidence before Completion | Critical |
| 9 | Riverlark | Post-completion release | Payout and releases at Completion | Critical |
| 10 | Bonuses (420k + on-costs) | Not in funds flow | Line item or seller-funded | High |
| 11 | Ironquay IP | Fee-only indemnity; "adequate" | Broaden; preserve cure; verify 180k | High |
| 12 | Export incident (DD-006) | "Not material" | Preserve, investigate, update; no assumptions | High |
| 13 | Sandbar (330k) | Ordinary course | Assess; no automatic Debt or deduction | Medium |
| 14 | Tax / IP | Settled under general regime | Open; separate; no unlimited liability | High |
| 15 | Title evidence | Share register (DD-012) | Independent evidence required | High |

**Immediate next steps:**
1. Obtain the full SPA draft to verify clause references.
2. Get a current data room index and bring-down of the disclosure letter (as at 22 September is stale).
3. Send Amelia Frost the list of Seller positions that sit at or beyond our fallbacks (cap at 20%, 18-month period, Riverlark post-completion release). Any concession needs her written authority, identifying the draft.
4. Reject the Seller's "FINAL / not to be re-opened" framing in the cover response, noting that the Seller's positions have not been agreed by Wattlebridge.
5. Obtain independent title, PPSR and Bluefen/Riverlark status evidence before we proceed further.
